s: With reference to the term ‘Samudra’ in the Rigveda, which one of the following is correct?
o: It necessarily refers to the open sea in every occurrence.
It denotes only the desert region called Dhanva.
It refers exclusively to the western sea mentioned in the Satapatha Brahmana.
It may denote a collection of water and need not necessarily mean the sea.
x: In the Rigveda, Samudra may refer to a collection of water and is not necessarily evidence of knowledge of the open sea in every occurrence.
tq: Distinguish the debated Rigvedic meaning from the later Brahmana reference to eastern and western seas.
sec: Physical features - Himavant, Mujavant, samudra debate

s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Rigveda from the Satapatha Brahmana regarding seas?
o: The Rigveda mentions only the eastern sea, whereas the Satapatha Brahmana mentions no sea.
The Satapatha Brahmana is earlier than the Rigveda and supplies the first reference to Dhanva.
The Rigveda uses Samudra in a potentially broad sense, while the Satapatha Brahmana refers to eastern and western seas.
Both texts use Samudra exclusively for the Arabian Sea.
x: The Rigvedic term Samudra has a debated, broad meaning, whereas the later Satapatha Brahmana mentions the eastern and western seas.
tq: Compare the textual usage of the same geographical idea across different Vedic layers.
sec: Physical features - Himavant, Mujavant, samudra debate

s: The Early Vedic period is generally dated approximately to which of the following periods?
x: The Early Vedic period is generally placed around 1500–1000 BCE, although some comparative tables use the narrower range 1500–1100 BCE.
tq: Select the conventional broad chronology while distinguishing it from narrower periodisations.
sec: Chronology and dating of the Rigveda

s: Which one of the following statements about the dating of the Rigveda is correct?
o: Astronomical dating is used exclusively to date the later Vedic period.
The Rigveda is universally dated only to the period after 600 BCE.
Indigenist scholars have used astronomical calculations to argue for an earlier date.
Michael Witzel rejected all textual layering and proposed a single short chronology.
x: Indigenist interpretations use astronomical dating to argue for an earlier Rigvedic chronology. Michael Witzel is associated with a Long Chronology of textual layers.
tq: Identify the correct scholar–approach association and reject absolute chronology claims.
sec: Chronology and dating of the Rigveda

s: Michael Witzel is associated with which approach to the chronology of the Rigvedic text?
o: The exclusively astronomical chronology of the Indus script
The Archaeological Culture Chronology of the Harappan cities
The Long Chronology of textual layers
The Short Chronology of a single-period composition
x: Michael Witzel proposed a Long Chronology that recognises different textual layers in the Rigveda.
tq: Use the scholar–concept pairing rather than confusing textual chronology with archaeological dating.
sec: Chronology and dating of the Rigveda

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the textual character of the Rigvedic Mandalas?

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Mandalas of the Rigveda is correct?
o: Mandala X is the earliest family book and contains no creation hymn.
Mandala VII is devoted entirely to Soma and Mandala IX contains the earliest family hymns.

s: Which one of the following statements best describes the relationship between Rigvedic evidence and archaeology?
o: The textual evidence has no connection with archaeological findings.
The rivers, tribes and settlements in the text broadly correspond with archaeological evidence, but the text requires critical reading.
Archaeology proves every episode in the Rigveda as a literal historical record.
The Rigveda is an archaeological report rather than a religious text.
x: Rigvedic references to rivers, tribes and settlements broadly correspond with archaeological evidence, but the religious text must be interpreted critically rather than treated as a literal chronicle.
tq: Avoid both extremes: neither dismiss the textual evidence nor treat every poetic passage as direct historical proof.
sec: Sources - Rigveda family books, archaeological correlates

s: The geographical importance of Sapta Sindhu lies primarily in the fact that it helps to identify which region as the Early Vedic heartland?

The Punjab–Haryana region and adjoining north-western areas
The eastern Deccan plateau and Tamil country
x: Sapta Sindhu geography places the Early Vedic heartland in Punjab, Haryana and adjoining north-western areas before the later eastward movement.
tq: Link the geographical cluster of rivers to the historical location of the Early Vedic culture.
sec: Universal angles

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the shift from the Early Vedic to the Later Vedic geographical core:
1. The Early Vedic core was located in Punjab and Haryana.
2. The Later Vedic core included the Ganga–Yamuna Doab, eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
3. Kosala and Videha formed part of the later eastern zone.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Early Vedic core lay in Punjab–Haryana, while the Later Vedic core shifted eastward to the Ganga–Yamuna Doab, eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, including Kosala and Videha.
tq: Compare the two cultural cores spatially and identify the direction of the eastward shift.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which one of the following sequences correctly represents the broad geographical movement of the Vedic cultural centre?
o: Punjab–Haryana to the Ganga–Yamuna Doab and then eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
Bihar to Punjab–Haryana and then eastern Afghanistan
Tamil country to the Indus valley and then the Ganga delta
Ganga delta to the Deccan and then Punjab–Haryana
x: The broad movement was eastward: from the Punjab–Haryana region to the Ganga–Yamuna Doab and subsequently toward eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
tq: Follow the directional sequence from the early north-western core to the later eastern core.
sec: Universal angles
